section_summary: This section records U.S. diplomatic reporting on Japan’s economic recovery, the depreciated yen, and the growing cost of military activity in Manchuria and China. Its central documents examine the 1933–34 budget, borrowing and bond issues, and warnings that military spending could undermine public support and financial stability. It also includes a translated budget, correspondence on Japanese dollar deposits, and file notes pointing to related records.

subfiles.title: Confidential enclosure letter to Marriner
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on an alleged French–Japanese alliance and the Lytton Report.
subfiles.summary: Confidential cover letter forwarding the November 22 conversation memorandum.

subfiles.title: Confidential enclosure letter to Grew
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the same conversation memorandum to the ambassador in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Confidential cover letter concerning the alleged alliance and Lytton Report.

subfiles.title: Confidential enclosure letter to Johnson
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the conversation memorandum to the minister in Peiping.
subfiles.summary: Confidential cover letter concerning the alleged alliance and Lytton Report.

subfiles.title: Confidential report on Japan’s monetary situation
subfiles.from: Warrington Dawson, forwarded by the American chargé d’affaires in Paris
subfiles.about: Comments on French press discussion of Japanese deflation and possible American inflation.
subfiles.summary: Dawson quotes praise for Japan’s avoidance of monetary inflation, then contrasts it with French press expectations that the incoming U.S. administration might use inflation to address its budget.

subfiles.title: State Department routing sheet
subfiles.about: Routes material concerning Japanese economic conditions.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing sheet with a request that the material be read.

subfiles.title: Comment on Japanese trade and yen depreciation
subfiles.about: Assesses criticism of Tokyo’s report against improving Japanese export and industrial figures.
subfiles.summary: Notes a rapid improvement in exports and industry after yen depreciation, despite earlier adverse reports.

subfiles.title: Comment on Tokyo despatch No. 201
subfiles.about: Warns that Tokyo’s account of Japanese prosperity may be overly optimistic.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the despatch’s prediction that temporary prosperity could end in a severe depression.

subfiles.title: Economic Conditions in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports industrial recovery, trade gains, yen depreciation, bond financing and risks of future collapse.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes sharply improved industrial output and exports following yen depreciation, with employment and business confidence recovering. He examines the note issue, gold cover, foreign payments and planned government bonds, concluding that substantial inflation is not yet inevitable. The proposed budget and military spending remain serious risks. He predicts that rising costs, tariffs, debt and overexpansion may eventually turn the current prosperity into a deeper depression.

subfiles.title: Summary of Tokyo despatch No. 211
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japan’s proposed 1933–34 budget and concerns about its military costs and borrowing.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum outlines the large budget, military allotments, expected bond issues and rising debt. It notes growing alarm among economic leaders and the public.

subfiles.title: Budget Estimates
subfiles.about: Analyzes the draft Japanese budget for 1933–34 and the borrowing needed to finance it.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a proposed general account budget of about ¥2.239 billion, including roughly ¥745 million in new undertakings. Tables detail departmental allotments, especially army and navy spending, and estimate borrowing of nearly ¥896 million, potentially more once other accounts are included. He describes the danger of debt financed military operations, opposition from business figures and party leaders, and Finance Minister Takahashi’s confidence in future revenue growth.

subfiles.title: Cover letter to Federal Reserve governor
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s telegram on possible transfers of Japanese dollar deposits to sterling.
subfiles.summary: Sends a copy of Grew’s March 3 telegram for information.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japan’s Financial and Economic Annual
subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of Japan’s 1932 Financial and Economic Annual.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter enclosing the Finance Department’s annual publication.

subfiles.title: Summary of reporting on public feeling toward the military
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese press criticism and a university professors’ meeting discussed in an Embassy despatch.
subfiles.summary: Notes warnings that military overreach and financial strain could erode public support.

subfiles.title: Comment on economic pressure and Japanese war psychology
subfiles.about: Disputes Wallace’s reading of an Embassy despatch about military popularity.
subfiles.summary: Argues that economic pressure would intensify Japanese war psychology and risk war.

subfiles.title: Public Feeling Regarding the Military
subfiles.about: Reports emerging criticism of military spending and encloses Goh’s speech, press translations and meeting notes.
subfiles.summary: Grew treats Baron Goh’s criticism of military expenditure as evidence that concern over the budget is weakening public support for the army. The enclosed speech discusses deficits, loans and the limited productive value of military spending; translated editorials warn against military interference in financial policy. W. T. Turner’s notes on a professors’ meeting suggest that some scholars resisted pressure to present a united front behind Japan’s overseas operations.

subfiles.title: Government Finance monthly report extract
subfiles.about: Recaps the proposed budget, debt and criticism of army and navy demands.
subfiles.summary: Monthly report extract on budget totals, debt and business concern about military appropriations.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese press claims about U.S. supplies
subfiles.about: Points to Grew’s telegram on claims that U.S. vehicles and aircraft were supplied to China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 17 under file 793.94/5766.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 17 on Japanese War Office claims
subfiles.about: Reports Embassy belief that the War Office promoted claims of U.S. supplies to China to support its budget request.
subfiles.summary: The War Office blurred private American sales with U.S. government action; the Embassy saw this as a bid for army funding.

subfiles.title: File note on next fiscal year’s budget
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Grew despatch about Japan’s next budget.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 245 in another file.

subfiles.title: File note on Diet budget debate
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Grew despatch on budget interpellations in the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 278 in another file.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 54 on Japanese dollar deposits
subfiles.about: Reports whether Japanese banks planned to transfer U.S. deposits into sterling.
subfiles.summary: Press reports suggested possible transfers, but Mitsui Bank’s president said it would keep dollar funds while New York conditions remained sound.

subfiles.title: Copy of cover letter to Federal Reserve governor
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Tokyo’s telegram about dollar fund transfers.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover letter for the March 3 telegram.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese foreign credit
subfiles.about: Points to Lamont’s letter on difficulty securing Japanese foreign credit after the Shanghai incident.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Thomas W. Lamont’s letter.

subfiles.title: Comment on translated Japanese budget bill
subfiles.about: Identifies Tokyo despatch No. 306 as a reference copy of the budget bill.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the bill was already discussed in despatch No. 211.

subfiles.title: Japanese Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning April 1, 1933
subfiles.about: Transmits an English translation of the general account budget bill.
subfiles.summary: Grew says the Lower House approved the bill and expects enactment without material amendment.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Money Market
subfiles.about: Identifies a consular report on the Japanese money market.
subfiles.summary: Title and approval sheet signed by Consul Arthur Garrels.

subfiles.title: Translation of the 1933–34 Japanese general account budget
subfiles.from: Japanese government; transmitted by Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.about: Sets out detailed ordinary and extraordinary revenues and departmental expenditures for fiscal 1933–34.
subfiles.summary: The translated bill itemizes taxes, state enterprise income and nearly ¥895 million in loans, with total revenue and expenditure of about ¥2.239 billion. It lists ordinary and extraordinary appropriations across government departments, including military equipment, Manchurian operations, public works, agriculture, transport and overseas administration. The surviving pages in this section end with the grand total.

subfiles.title: Cost of Japanese Military Activities in Manchuria and China
subfiles.about: Calculates the costs of Japanese military activity in Chinese territory and explains its loan financing.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy estimates costs through March 1934 at about ¥563 million, financed largely by loans taken up by the Bank of Japan and the Finance Department’s Deposit Bureau. An appendix reproduces the February 1933 supplementary budget for additional Manchurian spending.

subfiles.title: Summary card for despatch No. 304
subfiles.about: Summarizes the estimated cost and financing of Japanese military activities in Manchuria and China.
subfiles.summary: Records the ¥563 million estimate and ¥323 million already raised in loans.

subfiles.title: Government Finance monthly report extract
subfiles.about: Recaps Manchurian spending and a proposed increase in South Manchuria Railway capital.
subfiles.summary: Monthly report extract citing despatch No. 304 and Bank of Japan financing.

subfiles.title: Special Accounts Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning April 1, 1933
subfiles.about: Transmits an outline translation of Japan’s special accounts budget.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter linking the special accounts to the previously transmitted general account budget.

subfiles.title: Budget promulgation statement
subfiles.about: Promulgates the approved general and special account budgets for fiscal 1933–34.
subfiles.summary: Official sanction statement with countersignatures of the prime minister and cabinet ministers.
